hookLine: In Kentucky, a piece of paper fixed to a door was service. The question is whether the paper stayed up long enough to be read.

lines: A PAPER TAPED TO A DOOR

ACT_1.primary: LINNIE LINDSEY · BARBARA HODGENS · PAMELA RAY
ACT_1.secondary: Tenants in a Louisville housing project, 1975. Named once in the opinion, and not again.

lines: ONCE THE PAPER WAS ON THE DOOR,

ACT_1.secondary: The summary process a landlord uses to get possession back quickly. Speed is the point of it.
Jefferson County Sheriff. His deputies carried the writs.
Whether the statute, as applied to tenants in a public housing project, fails to afford them the notice the Fourteenth Amendment requires

lines: A HEARING YOU DO NOT KNOW ABOUT

ACT_1.quote: The fundamental requisite of due process of law is the opportunity to be heard.
ACT_1.attribution: Grannis v. Ordean (1914), quoted in Greene v. Lindsey

ACT_1.quote: little reality or worth unless one is informed that the matter is pending and can choose for himself whether to appear or default, acquiesce or contest
ACT_1.attribution: Mullane v. Central Hanover Bank & Trust (1950), quoted in Greene v. Lindsey

ACT_1.secondary: Two sentences. Almost everything turns on the order of the clauses.

ACT_1.primary: THE NOTICE SHALL STATE THE TIME AND PLACE OF MEETING OF THE COURT
ACT_1.secondary: The shortest sentence in the statute, and the reason the paper exists

lines: IT WENT ALL THE WAY DOWN.

ACT_1.label: Conversations on a doorstep, across all three apartments

ACT_2.quote: Posting refers to the practice of placing the writ on the property by use of a thumbtack, adhesive tape, or other means.
ACT_2.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey, 456 U.S. 444 (1982), n. 1 — defining the term

ACT_2.secondary: Personal service · a family member over sixteen · posting

lines: IF NO ONE ANSWERS THE DOOR,

ACT_2.quote: But if no one is at home at the time of that visit, as is apparently true in a good percentage of cases, posting follows forthwith.
ACT_2.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982) — the Court's own sentence; "good percentage" is quoted from a deposition, n. 8

ACT_2.quote: Neither the statute, nor the practice of the process servers, makes provision for even a second attempt at personal service, perhaps at some time of day when the tenant is more likely to be at home.
we reject appellants' characterization of the procedure

ACT_2.label: "a good percentage" — quoted from a deposition, not the Court's own estimate

ACT_2.quote: a singularly appropriate and effective way of ensuring that a person who cannot conveniently be served personally is actually apprised of proceedings against him
ACT_2.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), on what posting is in most cases

ACT_2.quote: It is, of course, reasonable to assume that a property owner will maintain superintendence of his property
ACT_2.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), restating why posting normally works

ACT_3.quote: Oh, we had plenty of trouble.
ACT_3.attribution: A process server, under oath, asked about children ripping the writs off — Greene v. Lindsey, n. 7

ACT_3.quote: I have seen them take them off of the door and I would go back and tell them to put it back. They don't know.

ACT_3.secondary: Named twice in the same footnote. The dissent gives the man who said "probably a couple of times" a name: Carter Bacon.

ACT_3.quote: the Housing Authority told us that they would take them off, so we always put them up high
ACT_3.attribution: A third deposition excerpt in the same footnote (App. 74)

ACT_3.quote: As the process servers were well aware, notices posted on apartment doors in the area where these tenants lived were not infrequently removed by children or other tenants before they could have their intended effect.

ACT_3.label: Studies, surveys or counts the majority weighed against the depositions

ACT_3.quote: and the six months I was working at it there was no occasion where I saw anyone tear the Writs off of the door
ACT_3.attribution: A process server, quoted only in the dissent

ACT_3.secondary: Same job, opposite answer. The dissent does not say they worked the same buildings.

ACT_3.quote: we always try to put the paper up above where, a, say a small child can't reach it
ACT_3.attribution: Another process server, quoted in the dissent

ACT_3.quote: claim never to have seen these posted summonses; they state that they did not learn of the eviction proceedings until they were served with writs of possession
ACT_3.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), Part I — the appellees' allegation

ACT_4.title: NO DOOR LEFT TO KNOCK ON

ACT_4.secondary: A class action under section 1983 — the statute that lets a citizen sue a state official for violating a constitutional right

ACT_4.quote: it was reasonable for the State to presume that a notice posted on the door of the building in dispute would give the tenant actual notice in time to contest the action
ACT_4.attribution: Weber (6th Cir. 1909), as described in Greene v. Lindsey

ACT_4.label: The year of Weber, the case the District Court leaned on

ACT_4.quote: there is undisputed testimony in this case that notices posted on the apartment doors of tenants are often removed by other tenants
ACT_4.attribution: The District Court, quoted in Greene v. Lindsey

ACT_4.quote: that posting only comes into play after the officer directed to serve notice cannot find the defendant on the premises
ACT_4.attribution: The District Court's ground, quoted in Greene v. Lindsey

items.label: The statute, read through the depositions

ACT_4.secondary: Reversed the summary judgment, and overruled its own 1909 decision to do it

ACT_4.quote: a time when posting provided a surer means of giving notice than did mailing. That time has passed.
ACT_4.attribution: The Sixth Circuit, quoted in Greene v. Lindsey — overruling Weber

ACT_4.secondary: Not decided. Sent back for further proceedings.

ACT_4.quote: Requiring Kentucky to provide notice by mail when personal service proves infeasible will not be overly burdensome. The cost will be minimal.
ACT_4.attribution: The Sixth Circuit, quoted in Greene v. Lindsey, n. 2

ACT_4.secondary: When notice is served by posting, a copy of the petition must be sent by registered or certified mail within a day

events.text: The Supreme Court notes probable jurisdiction

ACT_5.quote: appellees have been deprived of a significant interest in property: indeed, of the right to continued residence in their homes
the secure posting of a notice on the property of a person is likely to offer that property owner sufficient warning of the pendency of proceedings possibly affecting his interests
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), on why posting is normally enough

ACT_5.quote: But whatever the efficacy of posting in many cases, it is clear that, in the circumstances of this case, merely posting notice on an apartment door does not satisfy minimum standards of due process.
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey, 456 U.S. 444 (1982) — the turn

ACT_5.quote: Notice by mail in the circumstances of this case would surely go a long way toward providing the constitutionally required assurance
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), on the mails

ACT_5.quote: the State's continued exclusive reliance on an ineffective means of service is not notice reasonably calculated to reach those who could easily be informed by other means at hand
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), closing on Mullane's words

ACT_5.quote: In light of the findings of the courts below, we hold only that posted notice pursuant to section 454.030 is constitutionally inadequate.
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), n. 9 — stating its own limit

lines: IT DID NOT ORDER THE MAIL.

ACT_5.secondary: Joined by the Chief Justice and by Justice Rehnquist

ACT_5.quote: The sole ground for the Court's result is the scant and conflicting testimony of a handful of process servers in Kentucky. On this flimsy basis, the Court confidently overturns the work of the Kentucky Legislature and, by implication, that of at least 10 other States.

ACT_5.label: States, at least, authorizing notice in summary eviction proceedings solely by posting or by leaving it at the tenant's residence — the dissent's count

ACT_5.quote: As in Mullane, we decline to resolve the constitutional question based upon the determination whether the particular action is more properly characterized as one in rem or in personam.
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982) — the majority declining the category question

ACT_5.quote: we have long since discarded the concept that due process authorizes courts to hold laws unconstitutional when they believe the legislature has acted unwisely
ACT_5.attribution: The dissent, quoting Ferguson v. Skrupa (1963)

ACT_5.quote: It is no secret, after all, that unattended mailboxes are subject to plunder by thieves. Moreover, unlike the use of the mails, posting notice at least gives assurance that the notice has gotten as far as the tenant's door.

lines: SPEED IS NOT A DEFECT IN IT.

ACT_5.quote: from the perspective of the tenant, it is difficult to see how a means of serving process that fails to afford actual notice in a not insubstantial number of cases can be deemed either prompt or certain
ACT_5.attribution: Greene v. Lindsey (1982), n. 4 — the majority answering the dissent

ENDING.label: Studies, surveys or counts in the record. A handful of men describing their rounds.

ENDING.primary: A VERY SMALL PILE OF PAPER
ENDING.secondary: Set against a statute — and the three dissenting Justices said so

items.label: Rungs the men who climbed it described

lines: THE OPINION DOES NOT SAY WHICH.
THE PAPER WAS ON THE PREMISES.

_notes.script: episodes/_planning/EP62_greene_script.en.v003.md is the confirmed script. v001, v002 and v004 exist and must NOT be used. v003 is the verified pass: 77 verbatim runs checked against 456 U.S. 444 with zero fabrications and zero misattributions, ten logged defects closed, and the amicus attribution at line 247 corrected so that 'urged the Court to affirm' is scoped to the Antioch School of Law alone, which is what the reporter supports.
_notes.runtime: 5,271 extracted narration words (the script's own per-section labels sum to 5,250). design_speech_seconds in gen_narration_case.py is 1766 s, from the FINISHED rate of 178.35 words per finished minute measured on EP60 (178.4) and EP61 (178.3) -- a rate that already carries the pipeline's own inter-chunk gaps (143 s on EP60, 161 s on EP61). The 191-195 wpm raw speech rate is deliberately not used: it charges nothing for gaps and reports this script as short. Contract band 1620-1920 s.

EP60 and EP61 recorded only voice_id and model_id, so pace parity was unproven and check_script_length still reports a 237 wpm fast-end risk carried from two episodes whose settings had drifted.

Only 9 archive clips survived QC (47 ingested, 38 rejected on sight, 3 on shape/cross-episode reuse), which is the design, not a defect: 'front door', 'mailbox' and 'stairwell' return zero hits in a 140k-row archive. check_spec_satisfied counts only footage and remotion/public/greene/motion/*.mp4 towards distinct_video_assets (234), so the stills become assets only once they are in motion.
